findings.description: The new __init__.py guard assumes packaged test modules cannot collide. Pytest can import modules from separate package roots under the same qualified name. For example, hidden tests/hidden/pkg/test_x.py and agent-added tests/pkg/test_x.py both import as pkg.test_x when each pkg directory has __init__.py but their parents do not. The guard now preserves the agent-added collision that the previous implementation removed.
findings.failure_mode: Pytest collection aborts with an import-file mismatch or package import error, causing an otherwise correct solution to fail grading.
findings.suggested_fix: Determine each test module's pytest import name by walking contiguous __init__.py ancestors, and remove unowned agent files when that full import name collides with a protected module. Do not exempt every directory containing __init__.py.

findings.description: required = now + 2 * sum(watchdog_s over todo) / conc. Once todo is narrowed to the trials this invocation launches, the common --resume tail (one or two trials left) with concurrency > 2 yields a horizon shorter than a single trial's own watchdog. Example: one remaining trial with watchdog 16800 s at --concurrency 3 gives required_until = now + 11200 s, 5600 s before that trial can legitimately still be running its codex dissent step. The formula pre-dates this diff, but 1.2.x's narrowing of the sum makes the under-estimate the typical case rather than a corner case, and RAB-37 only exercises --concurrency 1 so the tests do not cover it.
findings.failure_mode: The pre-flight accepts a token that expires mid-trial on --resume; the codex dissent fails inside the trial, producing exactly the KF-048 transport/agent error the gate was added to prevent, and possibly tripping the outage breaker.
findings.suggested_fix: Bound the horizon below by the longest remaining trial: required = now + 2 * max(sum(w)/conc, max(w)) (or max(2*sum/conc, 2*max_w)). Update the header comment, the refusal text, and the RAB-31 expectation accordingly.

findings.description: write_status now passes --slurpfile cpf_f "$WORK/codex-preflight.json" on every call. That file is created only at pre-flight 6 and lives in the scratch dir. jq aborts with a non-zero exit when a --slurpfile path is missing, so any write_status call that precedes pre-flight 6 (for example a --clear-drift record or an early 'failed' state) or that runs from an EXIT/TERM path after $WORK is removed will fail. If the function redirects jq straight into STATUS.json the file is truncated to empty; if it writes via a temp file the status update is silently skipped. I could not see the call sites, so this needs a check of every write_status invocation and the trap ordering.
findings.failure_mode: STATUS.json is left empty or stale after a pre-flight-stage or shutdown-stage write, which then breaks the next --resume (the script reads STATUS.json for drift, cursor and rerun_pending).
findings.suggested_fix: Read the pre-flight JSON once into a shell variable right after it is produced (CODEX_PF_JSON="$(jq -c '.preflight' <<<"$CODEX_PF")", default 'null' before that point) and pass it with --argjson cpf "${CODEX_PF_JSON:-null}" so write_status has no filesystem dependency.

findings.description: remaining() re-derives the launch set as: plan entries with no row of this batch, plus --rerun ids, plus rows whose last status is in --rerun-status (minus --rerow ids). STATUS.json also carries rerun_pending (run_ids flagged on a previous invocation with no replacement yet) and a retries counter. If --resume relaunches pending reruns or auto-retries excluded rows, those trials have a row, are not in the CLI id list, and are not counted, so the horizon undercounts. Two smaller divergences: last-row-wins per run_id may differ from how the launcher picks the row a --rerun-status matches, and a row that parses but lacks the fields the launcher requires is treated here as 'rowed' while the launcher may relaunch it.
findings.failure_mode: On --resume the pre-flight reports trials_counted lower than the trials actually launched and accepts a token that expires before the extra trials finish; MANIFEST/STATUS record a misleading trials_counted.
findings.suggested_fix: Have the launcher write its actual launch list (run_ids) to $WORK before pre-flight 6 and feed that file to the Python instead of re-deriving the selection; at minimum include STATUS.json rerun_pending ids in the counted set and document the choice.

findings.description: PYTEST_FILES hardcodes pytest's default python_files (test_*.py, *_test.py) and the comment acknowledges the grader reads no pytest config. A fixture pytest.ini/tox.ini/setup.cfg/pyproject [tool.pytest.ini_options] with a custom python_files (or a hidden runner passing -o python_files=...) collects modules the grader does not treat as reserved. 1.2.11 reserved every .py basename and so covered this; 1.2.12 removes that coverage without checking any fixture config.
findings.failure_mode: A package-less agent module whose basename equals a non-default-named hidden test module survives; pytest's prepend import raises 'import file mismatch', collection aborts, and a correct solution scores 0/N on the hidden suite.
findings.suggested_fix: Parse python_files from the fixture's pytest config files (and the hidden runner's -o/-c arguments if any) with the two defaults as fallback, and feed the resulting patterns to collectable(); or, for fixtures whose config cannot be read, fall back to the 1.2.11 all-.py reservation restricted to package-less directories.

findings.description: The docstring states helpers never collide, which is true for the import-file-mismatch error but not for sys.modules shadowing. The 1.2.11 comment records that hidden suites rely on sibling imports resolved via sys.path (import _oracle_x, from helpers import ...). In prepend mode pytest inserts each package-less test module's directory at sys.path[0] and Python caches the first 'helpers' it imports. A package-less agent helper with a reserved-in-1.2.11 basename (e.g. tests/api/helpers.py beside tests/api/test_api.py doing 'from helpers import make_client') in a directory collected before the hidden dest (names sorting before 'hidden', such as tests/api, tests/cli, tests/core, tests/_util) is cached first; the hidden module's 'from helpers import slug_cases' then raises ImportError. 1.2.11 removed such a file; 1.2.12 keeps it. Narrow, and whether it is a strict regression depends on whether the hidden runner uses --continue-on-collection-errors, but it contradicts the stated rationale for dropping helper basenames.
findings.failure_mode: Hidden test module fails collection with ImportError on a correct solution; depending on runner flags the whole hidden run aborts or the hidden cases are silently absent from the count.
findings.suggested_fix: Keep non-collectable overlay/fixture-test helper basenames in a second set and remove an agent copy only when it is package-less AND its directory also contains a collectable test module (the only case pytest puts that directory on sys.path). This still protects the 1.2.11 failure case (src/app/helpers.py has no test module beside it). Alternatively, run the hidden suite with --continue-on-collection-errors and only the hidden paths, which removes the dependency on basename hygiene altogether.
